title: Fault Vignette Quickplay Card — compact failure + automatic retry simulation
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description: Design a compact, card-style debugging surface (Fault Vignette Quickplay Card) that surfaces a single failed request with key metadata, a condensed error taxonomy summary, the most relevant payload snippets, and an in-card automatic-retry simulator for reproducing transient failures. The card is intended for the Request List, Rollout Overview, and per-route error summaries where space is constrained.
goals: Allow engineers to triage common transient failures from a single compact surface without opening the full request detail view.
Provide an inline retry simulator that runs a safe, sandboxed reattempt and shows deterministic diffs (response status, latency, token delta) to speed TTR (time to repair).
Surface an explainable error taxonomy label (e.g., 'KV cache miss', 'kernel OOM', 'model-variant-fallback') with confidence and links to suggested mitigations.
user_flow: User scans Request List -> sees fault vignette card attached to failed request rows
Click expands minimal affordances: error summary, top-3 relevant payload snippets, retry button
Retry runs sandboxed call (no downstream side effects) and returns a short result bubble with outcome and a side-by-side micro-diff
User can escalate to full Request Detail or open the call in Replay mode from the card
acceptance_criteria: Card fits a 320px width column and remains legible at compact density
Retry simulator completes within 3s for cached quick-paths and returns deterministic outcome or explicit nondeterminism warning
Error taxonomy label computed or surfaced with tooltip explaining reasoning and a link to KB article
Accessibility: keyboard operable, ARIA role assigned, color-contrast >= AA
Performance: initial card render adds <40ms to request-list render in staging mock dataset
decisions: Retry simulator will call a 'safe-simulate' runtime endpoint that cannot mutate downstream state (decision from security review workshop 2026-02-28)
Default card density prioritizes the two highest-salience payload snippets; full payload opens in detail view to avoid exposing PII inline
Error taxonomy shown as single token + confidence. We will not attempt full root-cause inference in-card to avoid misleading signals.
tradeoffs: Compactness vs. context: To keep the card small we surface only 2 payload snippets which may omit the exact cause; mitigated with a direct 'Open in context' CTA
Simulator speed vs. determinism: quick simulated replays will optimize for fast failures detection but may not reproduce nondeterministic model outputs; we will surface nondeterminism warnings.
Privacy: Inline snippets will be redacted by default for flagged customers; this requires additional KMS rules (dependency).
